title: A computationally efficient algorithm for fitting ion channel parameters
author: Teed, Silva

steps.title: Na+ Voltage Dependent Activation
steps.instruction: From a resting potential of –100 mV, apply a series of depolarizing pulses ranging from –120 mV to 20 mV in 10 mV increments; for each pulse record the peak current and calculate conductance by dividing the peak current by the driving force (Vm − ENa).

steps.title: Na+ Steady‑State Inactivation
steps.instruction: Hold cells at –120 mV, then apply conditioning pulses from –120 mV to 20 mV in 10 mV increments, each lasting 200 ms; after each conditioning pulse step to –20 mV, record the peak current, and normalize each value by dividing by the maximum current observed.

steps.title: Na+ Recovery from Inactivation
steps.instruction: Hold cells at –120 mV, give a –20 mV depolarizing pulse for 200 ms, then allow recovery at –120 mV for durations ranging from 1 ms to 1000 ms; after each recovery interval apply a final –20 mV depolarizing pulse, record the peak current, and normalize across samples.

steps.title: Na+ Rise/Fall Time Measurement
steps.instruction: Repeat the Voltage Dependent Activation protocol; for each pulse measure the rise time as the interval for the current to increase from 10 % to 90 % of its maximum, and measure the fall time as the interval for the current to decline from 90 % to 20 % of its maximum.

steps.title: Na+ Conductance Trace
steps.instruction: Apply a single depolarizing pulse (conditions as in activation) and record the normalized conductance over a 5 ms recording window.

steps.title: K+ Voltage Dependent Activation
steps.instruction: From a resting potential of –100 mV, apply a series of depolarizing pulses ranging from –100 mV to 60 mV in 20 mV increments; for each pulse calculate conductance by dividing the peak current by the driving force (Vm − EK).

steps.title: K+ Deactivation Protocol
steps.instruction: Hold cells at –80 mV, then give a 60 mV depolarizing pulse for 2 ms; subsequently step to conditioning pulses ranging from –120 mV to 0 mV, each lasting 4 ms, and calculate conductance by dividing the minimum absolute current by the driving force (Vm − EK).

steps.title: K+ Rise Time Measurement
steps.instruction: Repeat the Voltage Dependent Activation protocol and measure the rise time as the interval for the current to increase from 10 % to 90 % of its peak value.

steps.title: K+ Conductance Traces
steps.instruction: Expose cells to depolarizing pulses of –20 mV, 0 mV, and 40 mV, and record the normalized conductance over a 4 ms interval for each pulse.
